findings.category: continuity — physical detail introduced by the repair pass
findings.gate: Craft core reader-trust invariant 3 (continuity persistence); shared positive voice — figurative language / description as selection

draft_evidence.quote: Two arms, the length of a hand, hinged at the top on a pin that turned without a sound … He opened them and closed them twice, and the pin made the small sound a pin makes that has been fitted by a man who fits pins for a living, and he put the points together and there was no light between them

comparison_evidence.quote: He opened it. The arms went apart without a sound, as a thing goes that has been made by a man who does not tolerate sound in a hinge, and stopped where the wheel held them

findings.consequence: The sentence added by the r2 pass says the pin makes a sound; the clause ninety words earlier in the same paragraph says the pin turns without one, and the next paragraph makes soundlessness the maker's signature — 'a man who does not tolerate sound in a hinge'. Three assertions about one hinge in twelve lines, two of them absolute and one of them opposite. The charitable reading (that 'the small sound a pin makes' names a near-silent, characteristic click) is available, but it has to be supplied by the reader against two flat 'without a sound' statements, and it is supplied at exactly the wrong moment: this is the paragraph where the chapter establishes that Hesk's work is exact and that Cael's way of loving a thing is to check it. A narrator whose whole characterization is that he counts correctly cannot describe the same pin twice, incompatibly, inside one breath of prose. The added sentence is otherwise a good beat and pays off B7 Ch24's 'no light under the line' — the defect is one clause inside it, not the beat. Secondary: the clause also puts a third 'small sound' into a chapter that already ends on one ('brass against brass, making their small sound', line 111) and uses it at line 33, which is the phrase's third appearance in 3,982 words.
findings.repair_target: Line 21, the added sentence only. Cut or replace the pin-sound clause and keep everything else in it: the two opens, the points put together, 'there was no light between them', and 'an instrument that closes true is the first thing you check and the only thing you cannot fix.' The check can be carried by what he sees or feels rather than hears — the pin's evenness under the thumb, the arms coming back to the same width — which also preserves line 23's soundlessness as the maker's signature and removes the third 'small sound' at no cost.

findings.category: line-level — sequencing and pronoun agreement introduced by the repair pass
findings.gate: Shared positive voice — sentence music; craft core, revision discipline (a repair should not create new friction)

draft_evidence.quote: He opened them and closed them twice, and the pin made the small sound

comparison_evidence.quote: He opened it. The arms went apart without a sound

findings.consequence: Before the repair, line 21 ended on 'a boy who watched' and line 23's 'He opened it' was the first time the tool was opened — a clean turn from watching to holding, and the paragraph break carried it. The insertion now opens the dividers at the end of line 21 and opens them again at the start of line 23, and switches the object's pronoun from plural to singular across the break ('opened them and closed them twice' → 'He opened it'). The reader is briefly unsure whether line 23 is a second, slower opening or a restatement of the first, and the emphasis that 'He opened it' used to carry — first contact — is spent one sentence early. This is small and local, but it sits in the chapter's best sequence and it did not exist in r1.
findings.repair_target: Line 21's added sentence and line 23's opening. Either move the check after line 23's slow opening (so the order is: he opens it, the arms go apart, then he closes them on themselves and finds no light between the points), or drop 'He opened them and closed them twice' from line 21 and let 'and he put the points together and there was no light between them' be the check, which needs no opening to precede it.

strengths: THE REPAIR PASS DID NOT SAND ANYTHING. The r1→r2 diff touches eleven lines and every one of them is a finding target or the sanctioned addition. The deniable plant, Seln's ledger, the family's register, the log's B7 Ch24 form, Karis's absence and the closing image all survive untouched or improved. This is the discipline the craft core's revision rule asks for and it is worth recording, because a repair pass that stays inside its lines is the reason r2 has only two findings rather than a fresh crop.

THE CAPPED-PHRASE FIX MADE THE BEAT BETTER, NOT MERELY LEGAL. 'For a count of one' [91] is a measure this narrator would actually use — he counts — where 'for the length of a breath' was a measure anyone would use. 'The space of a step' [97] is the log's register rather than the narration's, which is right for a line that is being filed. And the callback at [101], 'he had wanted, in that count of one, to go up the stair', now anchors the wanting to the exact instant of the wrongness instead of restating its duration. The chapter's own instruments did the work, exactly as the finding proposed.

'AN INSTRUMENT TURNING TOWARD HIM' IS THE STRONGER SENTENCE. Cutting 'the thing it was for' does not just protect Ch15 and Ch16 — it restores the beat's whole logic. The paragraph's argument is that Cael cannot say what happened, and the appositive was the narrator saying it for him. Now the pressure is described and left undescribed in the same clause, and [95]'s 'he did not have anything else to make it into and was not going to invent one' lands as characterization rather than as a hedge against a claim the prose already made.

THE ADDED CHECK RHYMES WITH THE STRAIGHTEDGE'S OWN FIRST CHECK. Line 21's 'he put the points together and there was no light between them, and he entered that, because an instrument that closes true is the first thing you check and the only thing you cannot fix' answers B7 Ch24's 'he sighted along it against the fire and there was no light under the line'. Two parcels, two objects, the same test, the same result, and the boy performing on the second what he watched being true of the first — that is the pairing the packet asked for, made physical. (One clause inside this sentence is F-CH14-R2-001; the beat itself should survive the repair.)

VASTIN'S EXCHANGE NOW HAS SOMETHING TO DISCLOSE. With the narrator's tables removed at [51], 'I have sat at a great many tables. I have never sat at one where the people who were not at it were counted' [63] is the first the reader hears of it, and 'The Compact counts who is present. It is very good at that' becomes the admission it was written to be. The replacement narration — 'the good manners of a man who had been served all his life and had never once been fed' — is doing different work from the line, not the same work early, which is what the finding asked for and more than it asked for.

THE CLOSER STOPS WHERE IT SHOULD. 'The light behind him, and the count in his head the whole way down, and he counted, and did not hurry, and the stair took him under' [113]. Cutting the because-clause leaves the discipline dramatized at [99] and [101] and enacted here, and the last four verbs are all acts. The chapter now ends on the image the card specified without explaining the image.

THE PLANT'S CALIBRATION SURVIVES INTACT AND IS NOW THE CLEANEST IN THE BOOK. He is not looking at it [91]; the wrongness is felt rather than seen; forty people on the street feel nothing [95]; the narrator refuses to theorize [95]; he waits for a second occurrence before entering the first as a pattern [99]; and he files it with the cord and the row rather than apart from them [97]. Escalation kit → row → light is legible in the log's own three-then-four count without a word of authorial pointing. Any Ch15 or Ch22 pass must leave this alone.

THE PROMISE IS STILL CHARGED, AND THE INTERVAL FIX MADE THE CHARGE LEGIBLE. 'Here was the first afternoon on which the thing she had asked for had cost him anything' [101] is unchanged in substance, and with 'eight days' now ruled and 'a winter' now true, the reader can date the cost: eight days of not-looking, one afternoon of wanting, one refusal. A rule became a value in one sentence and no one made a speech about it.

KARIS'S ABSENCE READS BETTER AT ONE DAY THAN AT THREE. 'A woman a day from the thing she had hunted her whole life was not a woman you went to see about' [9] is a sharper version of the r1 sentence, not merely a corrected one — the crew's restraint costs more when the thing is tomorrow, and the two cups at [43] then read as a shared position held for one more night rather than a standing habit.

READER STANDARD IS STILL MET BY CONDUCT RATHER THAN BY OMISSION. No oath, no coarseness, no violence, water at a celebratory meal, and the chapter's one dangerous object warned about plainly. What a thirteen-year-old actually gets here is a seat kept for someone who is not there, a promise held when holding it costs something, and an outsider fed and not told he is being included — three acts of decency, none of them announced, none of them free.
